  "hook": "Ramnista is Kir Yianni’s Naoussa Xinomavro that leans into the region’s limestone- and schist-influenced soils and strong diurnal swings to deliver high-acid, tannic red fruit rather than lush sweetness. The label’s repeated TEXSOM medals (golds in 2012 and 2015) mark a consistent stylistic statement across vintages.",
  "wine_summary": "This bottling matters because it represents Naoussa’s signature expression of Xinomavro: savory, tomato-skin acidity and firm tannins shaped by cool nights on the Vermio foothills. Kir Yianni helped professionalize modern Greek winemaking with temperature-controlled fermentation and more precise oak use; Ramnista follows that blueprint — a producer-level take on a regional grape rather than an experimental outlier. The medal run at TEXSOM across multiple vintages confirms the house style registers well with tasting panels and markets.",
  "terroir_expression": "Naoussa sits on the western foothills of the Vermio Mountains where calcareous (limestone) bedrock and patches of schist and clay-rich soils produce wines with lifted acidity and mineral spine; the continental climate with cold winters and warm days plus strong diurnal range preserves Xinomavro’s natural acidity and cultivates late-season phenolic ripeness, which is why Ramnista tastes of tart cherry, dried tomato, olive sap and an underlying mineral austerity linked to limestone and schist.",
  "vinification_summary": "Ramnista is made in a modern Naoussa style: controlled-temperature fermentation to retain primary aromatics, extended maceration to extract Xinomavro’s characteristic tannins (maceration is the time skins remain in contact with juice, which builds structure), and measured oak maturation to soften edges without masking savory fruit; these choices explain the wine’s bright acidity, firm tannic frame and restrained oak flavors.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Slow-roasted lamb kleftiko — the wine’s acidity and tannin cut through lamb fat while the herbal and mineral notes echo the dish’s oregano and lemon.",
    "Moussaka (eggplant, minced lamb, tomato, béchamel) — tomato-derived acidity in the dish mirrors Xinomavro’s tomato-skin tang, and tannins stand up to béchamel richness.",
    "Grilled pork souvlaki with charred lemon — char and citrus lift the wine’s savory, olive-like notes and the acidity refreshes the palate.",
    "Aged Kasseri or pecorino with quince paste — firm tannins and acidity balance the salty, tangy cheese and the quince complements the wine’s red-fruit and dried-fruit tendencies."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": "Thymiopoulos Naoussa — another modern-leaning Xinomavro that stresses bright acidity, mineral grip and transparent oak; Boutari Naoussa Reserve — a benchmark Naoussa with similar tannic structure and savory, tomato-like notes that show how producers differ chiefly in oak and extraction.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with high acidity, firm tannins and savory tomato/olive minerality",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now through the next 8–12 years for best balance between primary fruit and tertiary savory development; store at cellar temperature (12–14°C) on its side to keep cork moist.",
  "value_assessment": "Price: $29.46. At this price it competes with Thymiopoulos Naoussa and Boutari Naoussa Reserve in the $25–40 bracket; Ramnista is worth the money for buyers seeking a structured, food-friendly Xinomavro that emphasizes regional acidity and mineral character rather than plush ripeness.",
  "market_position": "Restaurants with focused Mediterranean lists and independent wine shops that promote Old World, food-driven reds stock this wine; the buyer is a guest or shopper seeking savory, ageable European reds rather than fruit-forward crowd-pleasers. Collectors will buy limited amounts for variety rather than large cellars.",
  "insider_take": "If you want a fruit-dominant, easy-drinking red, skip Ramnista; this is for people who prize structure and provenance — the payoff is in food pairing and medium-term bottle development. parsed.hook: Ramnista is Kir Yianni’s Naoussa Xinomavro that leans into the region’s limestone- and schist-influenced soils and strong diurnal swings to deliver high-acid, tannic red fruit rather than lush sweetness. The label’s repeated TEXSOM medals (golds in 2012 and 2015) mark a consistent stylistic statement across vintages.
parsed.wine_summary: This bottling matters because it represents Naoussa’s signature expression of Xinomavro: savory, tomato-skin acidity and firm tannins shaped by cool nights on the Vermio foothills. Kir Yianni helped professionalize modern Greek winemaking with temperature-controlled fermentation and more precise oak use; Ramnista follows that blueprint — a producer-level take on a regional grape rather than an experimental outlier. The medal run at TEXSOM across multiple vintages confirms the house style registers well with tasting panels and markets.
parsed.terroir_expression: Naoussa sits on the western foothills of the Vermio Mountains where calcareous (limestone) bedrock and patches of schist and clay-rich soils produce wines with lifted acidity and mineral spine; the continental climate with cold winters and warm days plus strong diurnal range preserves Xinomavro’s natural acidity and cultivates late-season phenolic ripeness, which is why Ramnista tastes of tart cherry, dried tomato, olive sap and an underlying mineral austerity linked to limestone and schist.
parsed.vinification_summary: Ramnista is made in a modern Naoussa style: controlled-temperature fermentation to retain primary aromatics, extended maceration to extract Xinomavro’s characteristic tannins (maceration is the time skins remain in contact with juice, which builds structure), and measured oak maturation to soften edges without masking savory fruit; these choices explain the wine’s bright acidity, firm tannic frame and restrained oak flavors.
food_pairing: Slow-roasted lamb kleftiko — the wine’s acidity and tannin cut through lamb fat while the herbal and mineral notes echo the dish’s oregano and lemon.
Moussaka (eggplant, minced lamb, tomato, béchamel) — tomato-derived acidity in the dish mirrors Xinomavro’s tomato-skin tang, and tannins stand up to béchamel richness.
Grilled pork souvlaki with charred lemon — char and citrus lift the wine’s savory, olive-like notes and the acidity refreshes the palate.
Aged Kasseri or pecorino with quince paste — firm tannins and acidity balance the salty, tangy cheese and the quince complements the wine’s red-fruit and dried-fruit tendencies.
parsed.comparable_wines: Thymiopoulos Naoussa — another modern-leaning Xinomavro that stresses bright acidity, mineral grip and transparent oak; Boutari Naoussa Reserve — a benchmark Naoussa with similar tannic structure and savory, tomato-like notes that show how producers differ chiefly in oak and extraction.
parsed.style_profile: Medium-bodied dry red with high acidity, firm tannins and savory tomato/olive minerality
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink now through the next 8–12 years for best balance between primary fruit and tertiary savory development; store at cellar temperature (12–14°C) on its side to keep cork moist.
parsed.value_assessment: Price: $29.46. At this price it competes with Thymiopoulos Naoussa and Boutari Naoussa Reserve in the $25–40 bracket; Ramnista is worth the money for buyers seeking a structured, food-friendly Xinomavro that emphasizes regional acidity and mineral character rather than plush ripeness.
parsed.market_position: Restaurants with focused Mediterranean lists and independent wine shops that promote Old World, food-driven reds stock this wine; the buyer is a guest or shopper seeking savory, ageable European reds rather than fruit-forward crowd-pleasers. Collectors will buy limited amounts for variety rather than large cellars.
parsed.insider_take: If you want a fruit-dominant, easy-drinking red, skip Ramnista; this is for people who prize structure and provenance — the payoff is in food pairing and medium-term bottle development. Many confuse Xinomavro’s tomato-skin acidity for under-ripe fruit, but here it’s intentional: the acid and tannin framework is the point.
